rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says al-baḥr here means fresh water, since salty seawater cannot grow pens; Arabs also called inland countryside a sea.
rows.anchor: مجاز البحر هاهنا الماء العذب يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads min baʿdihi as from behind it: seven seas flow into the freshwater sea.
rows.anchor: يمده من بعده أي من خلفه أي يسيل فيه سبعة أبحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats the clause as compressed, with an implicit phrase: even if God’s book were written with these pens and seas, it would not be exhausted.
rows.anchor: ومجازه مجاز المختصر الذي فيه ضمير، سبيله: فكتب كتاب الله بهذه الأقلام وبهذه البحور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating or resurrecting many is as easy for God as creating or resurrecting one; if He can raise one, He can raise more, since He only says Be and it is.
rows.anchor: إلا كخلق نفس واحدة وإلا كبعث نفس واحدة أي كإحياء نفس لأنه إذا قدر على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses the phrase as your brothers in the religious community.
rows.anchor: أي إخوانكم فى الملة وخرج مخرج فتى والجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes the related noun fatā has the plural forms fityān and fitya.
rows.anchor: وخرج مخرج فتى والجميع فتيان وفتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawālīkum means your paternal cousins and your patrons or guardians.
rows.anchor: «ومواليكم» (5) أي بنو عمكم وولاتكم..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses masṭūran as written and cites al-ʿAjjāj’s verse as poetic evidence for the root s-ṭ-r.
rows.anchor: «في الكتاب مسطورا» (6) أي مكتوبا قال العجاج:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zāghat means the eyes were bewildered, strained upward, or veered; he compares the wording with 53:17.
rows.anchor: «وإذ زاغت الأبصار» (10) أي حارت وطمحت وعدلت وفى آية أخرى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were tested and afflicted; the wording is related to earthquakes.
rows.anchor: أي ابتلوا وفتنوا ومنه الزلازل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yathrib is the name of a region and of the Prophet’s city; he cites Ḥassān’s pre-Islamic verse using the place name.
rows.anchor: «يثرب» (13) اسم أرض ومدينة النبي صلى الله عليه فى ناحية من يثرب قال حسان فى الجاهلية:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an open initial mīm, maqām means a place where you can stay; an anonymous verse uses al-maqāma for such a place.
rows.anchor: «لا مقام لكم» (13) مفتوحة الأول ومجازها: لا مكان لكم تقومون فيه ومنه قوله:

words: وَإِنَّا أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِي ضَلَالٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He paraphrases it as we are guided and you are in manifest error; Arabs can use aw where a coordinating wāw joins the paired terms, as in the cited line.
rows.anchor: لأن العرب تضع «أو» فى موضع واو الموالاة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say a speaker certain of his own faith uses this balanced wording sarcastically, knowing which side is guided; Abū al-Aswad’s conditional poem illustrates the posture.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم قد يتكلم بهذا من لا يشك فى دينه وقد علموا أنهم على هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaftaḥu baynanā means He judges between us.
rows.anchor: «ثم يفتح بيننا بالحق» (26) أي يحكم بيننا..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāffatan means for all people, universally.
rows.anchor: «وما أرسلناك إلا كافة للناس» (28) أي إلا عاما..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥṣaynāhu means We made it or recorded it.
rows.anchor: «وكل شيء أحصيناه» (12) أي جعلناه..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear register is a clear book.
rows.anchor: «في إمام مبين» (12) أي فى كتاب مبين..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzaznā means We strengthened and reinforced them; al-Namir ibn Tawlab’s line with ʿazat is cited as evidence.
rows.anchor: «فعززنا بثالث» (14) أي قوينا وشددنا قال النمر بن تولب:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the proverb man ʿazza bazza as the victor seizing what he wants, and bazza itself as taking away; ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib’s verse witnesses the usage.
rows.anchor: يقال فى المثل من عز بز : من قهر سلب وتفسير «بز» انتزع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Your ṭāʾir is your share of good or bad fortune.
rows.anchor: «قالوا طائركم معكم» (19) أي حظكم من الخير والشر..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs pronounce yā qawmi with kasra and omit the possessive yāʾ, just as they drop tanwīn in a singular vocative; he also cites a line of Zuhayr.
rows.anchor: بعض العرب يقول: يا قوم، يكسرها ولا يطلق ياء الاضافة كما حذفوا التنوين من نداء المفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle is originally lā; some Arabs add a pause hāʾ, producing lāh, which becomes tāʾ when connected.
rows.anchor: إنما هى «ولا» وبعض العرب تزيد فيها الهاء فتقول «لاه» فتزيد فيها هاء الوقف فإذا اتصلت صارت تاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manāṣ is escape or getting away, from nāṣa yanūṣu; ʿAmr ibn Shayʾ al-Asadī’s line attests lāta.
rows.anchor: والمناص مصدر ناص ينوص وهو المنجاة والفوت. قال عمرو بن شأى الأسدى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū al-Najm’s line glosses lā manāṣ as no movement or escape.
rows.anchor: آساد غيل حين لا مناص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUjāb means ʿajīb; Arabic can shift the pattern faʿīl to faʿāl, as in ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās’s poetic form sarāʿa for sarīʿa.
rows.anchor: «إن هذا لشيء عجاب» (5) مجازه مجاز عجيب وقد تحول العرب «فعيلا» إلى «فعال» قال عباس بن مرداس:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He defines ḥadhal in the eye as loss of the eyelash and burning of the eyelids, and notes that aḥfār can also mean eyelashes.
rows.anchor: والحذل فى العين سقوط الهدب واحتراق الأشفار، وقد قالوا للهدب أيضا «أشفار»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās’s line uses ḥadhalat for the eye.
rows.anchor: إنك عين حذلت مضاعه ... تبكى على جار بنى جداعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muʿaqqir ibn Ḥimār al-Bāriqī, whom Abū ʿUbayda identifies as blind, uses ḥadhal for the eye in his verse.
rows.anchor: فأخلفها الذى ظنت وقاظت ... ومأقى عينها حذل نطوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of yanābīʿ is yanbūʿ, a spring that gushes from the earth.
rows.anchor: «فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض» (21) واحدها ينبوع وهو ما جاش من الأرض..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When vegetation has dried up, it is said to have hāja; the earth hāja when its greenery dries.
rows.anchor: إذا ذوى الرطب كله فقد هاج ويقال: هاجت الأرض وهو إذا ذوى ما فيها من الخضر..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After turning yellow, it becomes broken, dried plant matter; ḥuṭām, rufāt, and darīn are equivalent words.
rows.anchor: بعد صفرته أي رفاتا والحطام والرفات والدرين واحد فى كلام العرب وهو ما يبس فتحات من النبات..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parts of the Book confirm one another and resemble one another.
rows.anchor: «متشابها» (23) يصدق بعضه بعضا ويشبه بعضه بعضا..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression is modeled on the image of an obstinate, contentious man.
rows.anchor: «ضرب الله مثلا رجلا فيه شركاء متشاكسون» (29) مجازها من الرجل الشكس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāliman means unshared or wholly one’s own; salima li-rajul means that something is reconciled or at peace for someone.
rows.anchor: «سالما» (29) خالصا وسلما لرجل أي صلحا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular relative expression stands for a group, both those who brought the truth and those who affirmed it; al-Ashhab ibn Rumayla’s line stresses the whole people.
rows.anchor: «والذي جاء بالصدق» (33) فى موضع الجميع وصدق به قال الأشهب ابن رميلة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā refers to a plurality, then is resumed by feminine hunna because the objects are lifeless idols; he links this to 4:116, where ināthan means lifeless things.
rows.anchor: ما هاهنا فى موضع الجميع مجازها مجاز الذي مثل بيت الأشهب هذا وقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qūt is provision: food, livelihood, and whatever is needed.
rows.anchor: «وقدر فيها أقواتها» (10) واحدها قوت وهى الأرزاق وما احتيج إليه..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the accusative in سواء للسائلين as an accusative of verbal noun.
rows.anchor: «في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين» (10) مجاز نصبها مجاز المصدر..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech attributed to the heavens and earth is a figure in which inanimate things, like animals, are described through actions modeled on human behavior.
rows.anchor: «قالتا أتينا طائعين» (11) هذا مجاز الموات والحيوان الذي يشبه تقدير فعله بفعل الآدميين..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says ḥifẓan is accusative on the same pattern as verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: «وزينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وحفظا» (12) مجاز نصبها كنصب المصادر..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarṣaran is a forceful, loud-sounding wind; Ibn Mayyāda’s line uses ṣarṣar for the destructive wind.
rows.anchor: «فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا» (16) الشديدة الصوت العاصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naḥisāt means ill-omened or unlucky.
rows.anchor: «نحسات» (16) ذوات نحوس أي مشاييم ..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hūn here means humiliation.
rows.anchor: «العذاب الهون» (17) أي الهوان..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūzaʿūn means they are driven or held back, from the verb wazaʿa.
rows.anchor: «يوزعون» (19) يدفعون مجازها يفعلون من وزعت ..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥamīm is a close relative or intimate.
rows.anchor: «كأنه ولى حميم» (34) الحميم القريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine plural pronoun refers to night, day, sun, and moon; after mentioning the sun and moon as objects of worship, the verse redirects worship to their Creator. Mixed or collective groups are expressed in the feminine.
rows.anchor: أي خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر فلما انتهى الكلام إلى الشمس والقمر وهما يعبدان نهى عن عبادتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a threat, not an order for people to commit unbelief.
rows.anchor: «اعملوا ما شئتم» (40) لم يأمرهم بعمل الكفر إنما هو توعد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akmām are the containers or sheaths from which things emerge; kamma is singular, and kam/kamma share the same meaning.
rows.anchor: «من أكمامها» (47) أي أوعيتها واحدها كمة وهو ما كانت فيه وكم وكمة واحد وجمعها أكمام وأكمة..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāṣa ʿanhu means he turned away from it.
rows.anchor: يقال: حاص عنه حاد عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both forms follow faʿūl: yaʾūs from yaʾisa and qanūṭ from qanaṭa; their meanings are the same.
rows.anchor: «يوس» (49) فعول من يئست.. «قنوط» (49) فعول من قنط ومجازهما واحد..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned away and moved far off from Me.
rows.anchor: «أعرض ونأى بجانبه» (51) أي تباعد عنى..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mawlā here is a paternal cousin, who cannot help another cousin.
rows.anchor: «يوم لا يغني مولى عن مولى شيئا» (41) ابن عم عن ابن عم..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunting titles call the condemned man what he was in worldly life.
rows.anchor: «ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم» (49) فى الدنيا..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawwajnāhum means We paired them with the maidens, like matching one shoe with another, two by two and all together.
rows.anchor: «وزوجناهم بحور عين» (54) جعلناهم أزواجا كما تزوج النعل بالنعل جعلناهم اثنين اثنين جميعا بجميع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āsin means changed in smell; people say that the water in a well has become āsin.
rows.anchor: «من ماء غير آسن» (15) الآسن المتغير الريح يقال: قد أسن ماء ركيتك..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min here functions as a plural expression.
rows.anchor: «ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك» (16) من هاهنا فى موضع جميع..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashrāṭ are signs or markers, so the Hour’s signs are its indicators; he also notes that a sheep’s ashrāṭ are small, poor-quality animals and cites Jarīr’s line.
rows.anchor: «فقد جاء أشراطها» (18) أعلامها وإنما سمى الشرط فيما نرى لأنهم أعلموا أنفسهم وأشراط المال صغار الغنم وشراره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwala lahum means he made it seem good or adorned it for them.
rows.anchor: «سول لهم» (25) زين لهم..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laḥn al-qawl is the implication or gist of speech; one may say someone is more adept at arguing than another.
rows.anchor: فى فحوى القول، يقال: فلان ألحن بحجته من فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here naʿlama means to distinguish.
rows.anchor: «حتى نعلم المجاهدين منكم والصابرين» (31) حتى نميز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means to weaken, from wahana yahinu.
rows.anchor: «فلا تهنوا» (35) وهن يهن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatrakum means He will not diminish or wrong you; Arabs say wataratnī ḥaqqī when someone wrongs them of their due.
rows.anchor: «ولن يتركم أعمالكم» (35) لن ينقصكم لن يظلمكم وترتنى حقى ظلمتنى..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥfānī and alḥafa mean to press someone insistently with a request; Abū al-Aswad’s line describes the importunate asker.
rows.anchor: «فيحفكم تبخلوا» (37) يقال: أحفانى بالمسألة وألحف على وألح قال أبو الأسود:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tajassus is investigation or searching, and he treats the related form tajassusū as equivalent; a person who does it is a jāsūs.
rows.anchor: وتجسسوا سواء والتجسس التبحث يقال رجل جاسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Ruʾba’s line, nāmūs and jāsūs mean the same; ʿawmaj is a snake and mansūs a watercourse, while ʿawmaja describes winding or irregular movement, as in al-ʿAjjāj’s torrent verse.
rows.anchor: الجاسوس والناموس واحد العومج: الحية والمنسوس المسيل وإنما سميت عومجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shaʿb is a broad tribal grouping, with qabāʾil below it; he illustrates the usage with Ibn Aḥmar’s lines and al-Kumayt’s image of Nizār’s many divisions.
rows.anchor: يقال: من أي شعب أنت؟ فيقول من مضر من ربيعة، والقبائل دون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-taʿārafū completes the preceding clause; inn akramakum starts a new sentence, while a connected construction would use an in an akramakum.
rows.anchor: من الآية الأولى ثم ابتدأت «إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم» (13) ولو عملت لقلت أن أكرمكم عند الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yudaʿʿūn means they are pushed; Arabs say daʿa fī qafāhu for pushing someone at the nape, as in 2:107. He notes a light form of yadaʿʿu al-yatīm.
rows.anchor: أي يدفعون، يقال: دعت فى قفاه أي دفعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is compressed; its full form is fa-yuqālu hādhihi al-nār, then it is said: this is the Fire.
rows.anchor: «دعا هذه النار» (13- 14) مختصر مخرجه: فيقال: هذه النار..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is not a question; it is a threat.
rows.anchor: «أفسحر هذا» (15) ليس باستفهام بل هو توعد..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For fakihīn, the accusative is permitted after the sentence is already complete; the meaning is enjoying themselves, and the form may instead be nominative.
rows.anchor: لأن نصبت مجازها مجاز الاستغناء فإذا استغنيت أن تخبر ثم جاء خبر بعد فإن شئت رفعت وإن شئت نصبت ومعناها: متفكهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports a reading fākihīn and explains its pattern like lābin and tāmir, meaning someone with much milk or many dates.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأها «فاكهين» فمجازها مجاز، «لابن» و «تامر» أي عنده لبن كثير وتمر كثير..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes the pairing to mean that the men of Paradise are matched with the houris; zawwij hādhā al-fard means make this single item into a pair.
rows.anchor: «وزوجناهم بحور عين» (20) مجازها: جعلنا ذكران أهل الجنة أزواجا بحور عين من النساء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-najm is grammatically singular but means the stars collectively; al-Rāʿī’s line about counting stars supports the collective sense.
rows.anchor: سم والنجم النجوم ذهب إلى لفظ الواحد وهو فى معنى الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghawā is from al-ghayy, and al-ghāwī is the person who strays.
rows.anchor: «وما غوى» (2) يغوى من الغى والغاوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports an alternative dialectal analysis, غوى يغوي like shaqiya yashqā; this usage is also said of a calf that becomes overfull or sick from milk.
rows.anchor: فهو من اللبن يبشم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes ʿan al-hawā to mean by desire or caprice.
rows.anchor: «وما ينطق عن الهوى» (3) أي ما ينطق بالهوى..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāba qawsayn means the measure or distance of two bows; qād, qayd, and qady are equivalent expressions.
rows.anchor: «قاب قوسين» (9) قدر قوسين وقاد، وقيد وقدى قوسين مثلها..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adnā means nearer.
rows.anchor: «أو أدنى» (9) أو أقرب..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-quwā is a collective term for strength.
rows.anchor: «شديد القوى» (5) جماع القوة..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhū mirra means possessing strength and firmness; a murr rope is tightly wound.
rows.anchor: «ذو مرة فاستوى» (6) ذو شدة وإحكام ، يقال: حبل ممر أي مشدود..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajinna is the plural of janīn, formed like sarīr and asirra.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع جنين، تقديره: سرير وأسرة..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akdā means he stopped giving; the word comes from reaching a hard layer while digging a well or saddle, then giving up.
rows.anchor: معنى أكدى: قطع، اشتقت من كدية الركية وكدية الرحل وهو أن يحفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿyahu means his work or deed.
rows.anchor: «وأن سعيه سوف يرى» (40) عمله..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tumnā means formed or determined; an Arab usage asks what the determiner has allotted for someone.
rows.anchor: إذا تخلق وتقدر، ويقال: ما تدرى ما يمنى لك المانى ما يقدر لك القادر..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next creation means bringing the dead back to life.
rows.anchor: «وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى» (47) يحيى الموتى:.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He enriched some people and gave them possessions or principal wealth.
rows.anchor: أغنى أقواما وجعل لهم قنية أصل مال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muʾtafika is the town that was overturned and sunk.
rows.anchor: «والمؤتفكة أهوى» (53) المؤتفكة المخسوف بها..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azifat al-āzifa means the Resurrection has drawn near.
rows.anchor: «أزفت الآزفة» (57) أي دنت القيامة..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāmidūn means heedless or distracted; an Arab says, leave off your heedlessness.
rows.anchor: «وأنتم سامدون» (61) لاهون، يقال: دع عنك سمودك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīmāhum means their identifying marks or signs.
rows.anchor: «يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم» (41) علاماتهم فى الأصل أعلامهم..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is elliptical: its full form is it is said, this is Hell.
rows.anchor: «هذه جهنم» (43) مجازها: [يقال] هذه جهنم..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ān is water that has reached its boiling point in intense heat; anything that reaches its limit is called ān. He compares 33:53 and cites al-Nābigha for ān meaning arrived or attained.
rows.anchor: بلغ إناه فى شدة الحر وكل مدرك آن وفى آية أخرى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afnān means branches.
rows.anchor: «ذواتا أفنان» (48) أي أغصان..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istabraq names a Chinese textile, neither as thick as brocade nor as light as farand.
rows.anchor: «من إستبرق» (54) يسمى المتاع الصيني الذي ليس له صفاقة الديباج ولا خفة الفرند إستبرقا ..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden fruit is near enough to gather; the phrase does not refer to the person gathering it.
rows.anchor: «وجنى الجنتين دان» (54) ما يجتنى قريبا لا يعنى الجاني..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not raise or stretch their gaze.
rows.anchor: «قاصرات الطرف» (56) لا تطمح أبصارهن..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaṭmith means to touch; Arabs say a camel has never been touched by a rope.
rows.anchor: لم يمسسهن، يقال: ما طمث هذا البعير حبل قط أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies al-wāqiʿa with the Hour, which is also called the approaching event in 53:57.
rows.anchor: «إذا وقعت الواقعة» (1) «أزفت الآزفة» (53/ 57) وهى القيامة والساعة..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He attaches khāfiḍatan rāfiʿatan to the earlier statement; if it continued the later clause, it would be accusative. Arabic can shift repeated news from accusative to nominative, as in 70:15–17 and the anonymous rajaz verse.
rows.anchor: العرب إذا كرروا الأخبار وأعادوها أخرجوها من النصب إلى الرفع فرفعوا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rujjat means it shook or quaked; an arrow is also said to vibrate in the target.
rows.anchor: «إذا رجت الأرض رجا» (4) اضطربت والسهم يرتج فى الغرض ..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are mashed like moistened sawīq or dough; a Ghatafān thief, afraid he would run out of time to bake, wet the flour and ate it as dough, as in his line.
rows.anchor: «وبست الجبال بسا» (5) مجازها كمجاز السويق المبسوس أي المبلول والعجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn and the Pen are treated like the other opening letters of the sūras.
rows.anchor: «ن والقلم» (1) كسائر فواتح السور..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasṭurūn means they write; Ruʾba’s line with asṭār is cited for the usage.
rows.anchor: إنى وأسطار سطرن سطرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He paraphrases it as which of you is possessed, comparing the construction with an early poet’s line about the sons of Jaʿda.
rows.anchor: مجازها: أيكم المفتون كما قال الأول :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tud’hin comes from mudāhana, acting with insincere accommodation or flattery.
rows.anchor: «لو تدهن» (9) من المداهنة..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse ʿutull means a coarse, foul unbeliever; more generally it means strong in any respect. Dhū al-Iṣbaʿ al-ʿAdwānī uses muʿtallan for strong.
rows.anchor: العتل الفظ الكافر فى هذا الموضع وهو الشديد فى كل شىء قال ذو الإصبع العدوانى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿda dhālika means in addition to that.
rows.anchor: «بعد ذلك» (13) مع ذلك..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zanīm is someone attached to a clan but not truly of it; Ḥassān ibn Thābit’s verse uses the term, which also names a he-goat with two wattles.
rows.anchor: الزنيم المعلق فى القوم ليس منهم قال حسان بن ثابت:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarhaquhum means it covers or overtakes them.
rows.anchor: «ترهقهم» (43) تغشاهم..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makẓūm means grief-stricken, like kaẓīm.
rows.anchor: «مكظوم » (48) من الغم مثل كظيم..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿarāʾ is the exposed face of the ground; Qays ibn Jaʿda of Khuzāʿa uses it in a poem about casting clothing into open country.
rows.anchor: لألقى بوجه الأرض قال رجل من خزاعة يقال له قيس ابن جعدة أحد الفزارين:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuzliqūnaka means to dislodge or knock you off; the related forms are all from the idea of slipping.
rows.anchor: ليزلقونك» (51) ولينقذونك وكل ذاك إزلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭāghiya means their transgression and unbelief.
rows.anchor: «فأهلكوا بالطاغية» (5) بطغيانهم وكفرهم..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakhkharahā ʿalayhim means He kept the wind going against them without pause; ḥusūman means successive.
rows.anchor: أدامها عليهم ليس فيها فتور. «حسوما» (7) متتابعة ..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿjāz are the trunks or bases; the feminine form khāwiya reflects the dialect that treats nakhl as feminine.
rows.anchor: «أعجاز نخل خاوية» (7) أصولها، مجازها لغة من أنث النخل..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāqiya means remnant and is a verbal noun on the pattern of ṭāghiya; verbal nouns rarely take the fāʿila pattern, with examples including maysūr, maʿsūr, and maʿqūl.
rows.anchor: من بقية ومجازها مجاز الطاغية مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rābiya means increasing, growing, and severe, from rabāʾ, growth.
rows.anchor: «أخذة رابية» (10) نامية زائدة شديدة من الرباء..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿīhā derives from waʿā, to retain or understand.
rows.anchor: «وتعيها أذن واعية» (12) من وعيت..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verbal noun is used adjectivally, it follows the pattern of a noun whose agent is unmentioned; without the adjective, one would say ḍuriba ḍarban.
rows.anchor: لما جاءت المصادر صفة جرى على مجرى الاسم الذي لم يذكر فاعله ولو جاء بغير صفة لقلت: ضرب ضربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥamīm is a close relative or intimate.
rows.anchor: «ولا يسئل حميم حميما» (10) قريب قريبا..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on the mīm, the punishment is annexed to the day and the day to idh; with fatḥa, the mīm belongs inside the word and idh is declined and nunated.
rows.anchor: فمن جر الميم أضاف العذاب إلى اليوم إلى إذ ومن فتح الميم جعل الميم حرفا من وسطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faṣīla is a smaller group than a tribe, a clan or sub-clan that shelters its members; the sequence runs from broad shaʿb through tribes to faṣīla.
rows.anchor: «وفصيلته التي تؤويه» (13) دون القبيلة، الشعوب أكثر من القبائل ثم الفصيلة، فخذه التى تؤويه ..

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For humans, shawāt are the hands, feet, and head; al-Aʿshā’s word shawātahu is corrected by Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ to sarātahu.
rows.anchor: واحدتها شواة وهى اليدان والرجلان والرأس من الآدميين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports hearing a man in Medina say iqshaʿarrat shawātī, my limbs bristled, as evidence for the human use of shawā.
rows.anchor: وسمعت رجلا من أهل المدينة يقول اقشعرت شواتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a horse, shawā means its legs, as in ʿablu al-shawā; it is not used for the head, since horses are praised for slender cheeks and a refined face.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون هذا للرأس لأنهم وصفوا الخيل بأسالة الخدين وعتق الوجه ورقته
